articles.title: किमदेखि एलिनसम्म : विदेशीको भिसा, विवाह र गतिविधिको डरलाग्दो रिपोर्ट
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । विदेशी नागरिक नेपाल घुम्न, व्यापार गर्न वा अध्ययनका लागि आउने गरेका छन् । तर अध्यागमन र सुरक्षा निकायको अनुसन्धानले यसरी आउने केही विवाह, भाषा केन्द्र र एनजीओको आवरणमा धार्मिक प्रचारदेखि शंकास्पद गतिविधिसम्म गरेको देखाएको छ । पिटर क्वाङ सियोङ किमदेखि एलिन बिट ब्रोगस्ट्रोमसम्मका घटनाले राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामाथि गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएको छ ।

विदेशी नागरिक नेपाल किन आउँछन् ? यसको सामान्य जवाफ हा घुम्न, व्यापार गर्न, अध्ययन गर्न, व्यवसाय गर्न वा नेपालमा केही समय बस्न । तर अध्यागमन विभाग र सुरक्षा निकायको अनुसन्धानले केही विदेशीको नेपाल बसाइँको उद्देश्य सामान्यभन्दा निकै फरक र गम्भीर हुनसक्ने देखाएको छ । यसको एउटा उद्धाहरण हुन्, दक्षिण कोरियाली मूलका अमेरिकी नागरिक पिटर क्वाङ सियोङ किम । उनी विगत एक महिनादेखि अध्यागमन विभागको हिरासतमा थिए । तर सर्वोच्च अदालतले बन्दीप्रत्यक्षीकरण रिटमाथि फैसला गर्दै उनलाई थुनामुक्त गर्न आदेश दिएको छ ।

किम सन् २०१३ देखि नेपाल आउजाउ गर्दै आएका थिए । नेपाली महिला निलम बर्देवासँग विवाह गरेपछि उनले वैवाहिक भिसासमेत लिएका थिए । तर अध्यागमन विभागले उनलाई साउनमा एक वर्ष नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न नपाउने गरी देश निकाला गरेको थियो ।

त्यसविरुद्ध उनकी श्रीमतीले सर्वोच्चमा रिट दायर गरेकी थिइन् । किममाथिको अनुसन्धानमा भने उनको गतिविधि धार्मिक प्रचार, भिसाको दुरुपयोग र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षासँग जोडिएको विषयमा केन्द्रित देखिन्छ । अनुसन्धान अनुसार किमले दोलखाको चरिकोटमा भाषा केन्द्र सञ्चालन गरेका थिए ।

सन् २०१८ मा भीमेश्वर बहिरा आधारभूत विद्यालयमा क्रिश्चियन धर्म प्रचार गरेको र तत्कालीन प्रधानाध्यापकलाई धर्म परिवर्तन गराएको आरोपसमेत अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ । काभ्रेको नमोबुद्धमा रहेको द लाइट एन्ड सल्ट स्कुलमार्फत् विपन्न बालबालिकालाई लक्षित गरेर धर्म प्रचार गरिएको दाबी पनि गरिएको छ ।

त्यस्तै दोलखा, सिन्धुली र काभ्रेमा धार्मिक गतिविधि विस्तार गर्ने, स्थानीय अवस्था र भविष्यमा लगानी गर्नुपर्ने क्षेत्रबारे रिपोर्ट तयार पारेर विदेशस्थित संस्थामा पठाउने गरेको अनुसन्धानमा भेटिएको बताइएको छ । यसका लागि उनले अमेरिकामा रहेका संस्थाहरुबाट आर्थिक सहयोग पाउने गरेका थिए ।

मिसनरी कार्यलाई निरन्तरता दिनकै लागि रणनीतिक रूपमा उनले व्यावसायिक भिसालाई विवाह भिसामा परिणत गर्ने योजना बनाएको देखिन्छ । उनको वैवाहिक सम्बन्ध नेपालमा दीर्घकालीन बसोवास गर्ने र आफ्नो कानुनी हैसियत जोगाउन मात्र प्रयोग भएको देखिन्छ ।

अनुसन्धानमा सन् २०२२ को नेपाल मिसन रिपोर्ट पनि फेला परेको बताइएको छ । बिजनेस भिसामा बस्दा उनले गरेको गतिविधि थाहा पाएर डिपोर्ट हुनसक्ने जोखिमका कारण वैवाहिक भिसा लिने योजना बनाइएको २०२२ नेपाल मिसन रिपोर्टमा उल्लेख भएको अध्यागमनको दाबी छ । किम ७२ वर्षका र उनकी नेपाली श्रीमती ३० वर्षकी रहेको तथा किमको अमेरिकामा समेत परिवार र सन्तान रहेको अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ ।

किमजस्तै अरु को को ?

तर यस्तो विषय किममा मात्रै सीमित छैन । स्वीडेनी नागरिक एलिन बिट ब्रोगस्ट्रोमको विषय पनि अनुसन्धानमा आएको छ । ५१ वर्षीया एलिनले २४ वर्षीय वीरगञ्ज घर भएका अनिकेतकुमार डंगोलसँग २०७९ भदौ ६ गते काठमाडौँ जिल्ल्ला अदालतबाट विवाह गरी त्यसैको आधारमा जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय पर्साबाट नेपाली अंगीकृत नागरिकता लिएको र त्यसपछि सम्बन्धविच्छेद गरेको अनुसन्धानमा देखिएको छ ।

अनुसन्धान अनुसार दुवैबीच खासै चिनजान थिएन र विवाहपछि पनि श्रीमान श्रीमतीको रूपमा बसेको पनि देखिएन । आर्थिक प्रलोभनमा कागजी विवाह भएको आशंका गरिएको छ ।

एलिनले पछि अर्का विदेशी नागरिकसँग विवाह गरिन् र उनलाई समेत नेपाल ल्याएको अनुसन्धानमा भेटिएको छ । उनले स्वीडेनी नागरिकता त्यागेको दाबी गरेपनि त्यसको प्रमाण पेस नगरेको बताइन्छ । नेपाली राहदानी प्रयोग गरेर भारत १६ पटक गएको र त्यहाँबाट स्वीडिस राहदानीमार्फत तेस्रो मुलुक गएको विवरणसमेत अनुसन्धानमा आएको छ ।

एलिनका विदेशी श्रीमानले गोफिका इन्टरनेसनल कार्गो प्रालि नामको कम्पनी २०८० जेठ १४ गते उद्योग विभागमा दर्ता कम्पनी खोलेर बिजनेस भिसा लिएको तर कारोबार नगरी कम्पनी बन्द गरेको विवरण पनि अनुसन्धानमा छ । नेपाली नागरिकता लिएकी एलिनले नेपाली युवासँग सम्बन्ध बिच्छेद गरी पुन आफ्नै श्रीमानसँग विवाह गरेको पाइएको छ । यसै विवाहको आधारमा उनले श्रीमान कार्ललाई समेत नेपाली अंगिकृत नागरिकता समेत दिलाउन सफल भएको पाइन्छ । एलिनसँग नेपालमा विहे गर्नु अघि कार्ल ११ पटक पर्यटक र ५ पटक व्यवसायिक भिसामा नेपाल आइसकेका थिए ।

एलिनका श्रीमानले नेपाली अंगीकृत नागरिकता लिँदासम्मको सबै विवरणहरू शंकास्पद रहेको देखिन्छ । यसबारे राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागले अनुसन्धान गरेर रिपोर्ट पनि दिएको छ । तर कानुनी रूपमा उनीहरूले सबै प्रक्रिया पूरा गरेर नेपाली नागरिकता समेत लिएकाले कारबाही प्रक्रिया भने अघि बढाउन सकेको छैनन ।

अर्को उदाहरण अमेरिकी नागरिक अमान्ड मैडा समर्स हुन् । उनले ९२ वर्षीय हर्कबहादुर घर्तीसँग विवाह गरेर वैवाहिक भिसामा नेपाल बसेकी थिइन् । उनी १५ वर्षजति नेपालमा बसेकी थिइन् ।

विवाहपछि अमान्ड ललितपुर महानगरपालिका–२५, सैंबुमा बसिन् र सन्ध्या कर्णको नाममा दर्ता भएको स्वालम्बन नामक एनजीओमा आबद्ध भइन् । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा उनले पाकिस्तानी नागरिक लर्ड किङ भिन्सेन्टलाई नेपालमा सेल्टर दिएको खुलेको बताइएको छ । भिन्सेन्ट २०२५ जनवरी २८ मा नेपाल आएका थिए र उनको पर्यटक भिसा मे १२ सम्म मात्रै थियो । तर भिसा सकिएको करिब एक महिनासम्म अमान्डले उनलाई आश्रय दिएको अनुसन्धानमा भेटियो ।

गुप्तचर सूचनाका आधारमा २०८३ जेठ २९ गते सैंबुबाट उनीहरू पक्राउ परे र पछि डिपोर्ट गरिए । अध्यागमन विभागका अनुसार सन् २०२५ मा मात्रै ५२३ विदेशी नागरिक डिपोर्ट भएका छन् ।

तीमध्ये चीनका १२०, बंगलादेशका ७५, अमेरिकाका ३५, बेलायतका २२, पाकिस्तानका १८ र अन्य देशका २५३ नागरिक छन् । ४५९ जना ओभरस्टे र ६४ जना शंकास्पद गतिविधिका कारण डिपोर्ट गरिएको विभागको तथ्यांक छ ।

यसरी डिपोर्ट गरिएकाहरु मध्यै धेरैले पहिला अध्ययन भिसा, व्यवसायिक भिसाको बहानामा लामो समय नेपालमा बसेर मिसनरीको रूपमा काम गर्ने प्रवृत्ति देखिएको छ । काठमाडौंलाई नेस्ट अफ स्पाई भनिन्छ । विभिन्न देशका गुप्तचर एजेन्सीहरूको ट्रान्जिट र सूचना संकलन केन्द्रका रूपमा समेत काठमाडौंलाई प्रयोग गर्ने गरिएको सुरक्षा विश्लेषण छ ।

नेपालमा हुने गतिविधिमा चिनियाँ चासो वा अमेरिकी रणनीतिक उद्देश्यका लागि सूचना संकलनका काम गरेको हुनसक्ने सुरक्षा संयन्त्रको विश्लेषण छ । त्यसैले पर्यटन, व्यवसाय, भाषा केन्द्र, एनजीओ वा विवाहको आवरणमा लामो समय बस्ने र त्यस क्रममा धार्मिक प्रचार, शंकास्पद गतिविधि वा राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामा असर पार्ने काम हुन सक्ने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: ‘गोदावरी महिला उद्यम विकास प्रतिष्ठान’को उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गोदावरी नगरपालिकामा नवनिर्मित ‘गोदावरी महिला उद्यम विकास प्रतिष्ठान’को आइतबार एक विशेष समारोहबीच उद्घाटन गरिएको छ ।

महिलाहरूलाई सीप विकास, उद्यमशीलता र आयआर्जनका अवसरहरूसँग जोड्दै आर्थिक रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बनाउने उद्देश्यले प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना गरिएको हो । गोदावरी नगरपालिकाका उपप्रमुख मुना अधिकारीको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त कार्यक्रममा नगर प्रमुख गजेन्द्र महर्जन प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी थिए ।

कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वडाका वडाध्यक्ष, जनप्रतिनिधि, महिला उद्यमी, सरोकारवाला संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि तथा स्थानीयको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो । समारोहमा स्थानीय महिला उद्यमीहरूले उत्पादन गरेका विभिन्न सामग्रीको प्रदर्शनीसमेत गरिएको थियो ।

नवनिर्मित प्रतिष्ठानलाई महिला उद्यमीहरूका लागि तालिम, उत्पादन, प्रदर्शनी तथा बजारीकरणको एकीकृत केन्द्रका रूपमा विकास गर्ने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

गोदावरी नगरपालिकाले महिलाहरूलाई शिक्षा, सीप र उद्यमशीलतामार्फत आत्मनिर्भर बनाउन अनौपचारिक शिक्षा कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन कार्यविधि २०८१ समेत जारी गरी अभियान सञ्चालन गरिरहेको छ । हालसम्म ४७ जना महिलाले प्लस टु उत्तीर्ण गरिसकेका छन् भने ११ जना स्नातक तहमा अध्ययनरत छन् ।

यस्तै, १४० भन्दा बढी महिला तह १ र २ मा अध्ययन गरिरहेका छन् । शिक्षाका साथै महिलाहरूलाई आयआर्जनमा जोड्न नगरपालिकाले ढाका बुनाई, साबुन तथा सरसफाइ सामग्री निर्माण, सिलाइ–कटाइ, हस्तकला, अचार, टपरी र स्यानिटरी प्याड उत्पादनजस्ता विभिन्न सीपमूलक तालिमहरू सञ्चालन गर्दै आएको छ ।

महिलाहरूलाई केवल तालिममा मात्र सीमित नराखी शिक्षित, सीपयुक्त, स्वरोजगार र पूर्ण रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बनाउनु यस अभियानको लक्ष्य रहेको छ ।

articles.title: दोलखामा दिनभर धार्मिक परिक्रमा, रातभर लाखे नाच !
articles.summary:
दोलखा । प्राचीन तथा ऐतिहासिक नगरी दोलखामा धार्मिक सहिष्णुता र सांस्कृतिक सद्भावको प्रतीक मानिने परम्परागत हिले जात्रा अर्थात् गुउँला पर्व हर्षोल्लासका साथ मनाइँदैछ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदा अर्थात् घण्टाकर्ण (गाठामा) को तेस्रो दिनदेखि सुरु भएको यो ऐतिहासिक पर्वका कारण यतिबेला दोलखा बजार २४ सै घण्टा सांस्कृतिक रौनकमा झुमिरहेको छ ।

बिहानैदेखि गुञ्जने परम्परागत बाजा, धार्मिक परिक्रमा र दिउँसोदेखि रातिसम्म देखाइने फरक स्वरूपका लाखे नाचले प्राचीन नगरी दोलखा यतिबेला गुञ्जायमान बनेको छ । घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् स्थानीय भाषामा ‘गाठामा’को तेस्रो दिन, श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि दोलखामा गुउँला जात्राको औपचारिक सुरुवात हुन्छ ।

माथिल्लो र तल्लो टोलका बेग्लाबेग्लै डापा खलक परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित बिहानै सांस्कृतिक परिक्रमामा निस्कन्छन् । स्थानीय भाषामा देउ उय भनिने यो परिक्रमा कागे अष्टमीका दिन समापन हुन्छ ।

पूजा सामग्री बोकेका ज्येष्ठ नागरिकसहितको टोली स्वयंभू चैत्य र कोर्छे टोलबाट सुरु भई भीमेश्वर, कालीमन्दिर, त्रिपुरा सुन्दरी, राजकुलेश्वर तलेजु, नक्छे चैत्य, गणेश मन्दिर र मच्चिछन्द्रनाथ मन्दिर हुँदै पुनः स्वयंभू चैत्य पुगेर टुंगिन्छ । जात्रा मनाउँदा हिन्दू र बौद्ध दुवै धार्मिकस्थलको समान रूपमा परिक्रमा गरिन्छ ।

दिउँसोदेखि दोलखा बजारमा लाखे नाचको रौनक सुरु हुन्छ । एउटै जात्रामा चार फरक स्वरूपका लाखे प्रदर्शन हुने भएकाले दोलखाको लाखे देशभरमै विशेष मानिन्छ ।

दिउँसो ३ देखि ५ बजेसम्म ‘जोङ डाकस’ निकालिन्छ । यसमा हात दुई जना दाउरेले समातेर दर्शकलाई लखेट्दै मनोरञ्जन गराउँछन् । आसुरी शक्तिमाथि विजयको कथा भन्ने नेपाल डाकस भने राति मात्र नाचिन्छ । वर्षमा एक दिन रक्षाबन्धनका दिन निकालिने ‘ड्वाकु डाकस’ ठूलो लाखे हो । फरक मुखुण्डो लगाइने यसलाई महाकालीका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ ।

गाईजात्रादेखि पञ्चमीसम्म ‘माझीपा डाकस’ पनि प्रदर्शन गरिन्छ । डोरीले बाँधेर लाखेलाई नचाउने र माझीहरूले नियन्त्रण गर्न खोजेको लोककथाको अभिनय यसमा देखाइन्छ । पुस्तौँदेखि चल्दै आएको यस अमूर्त कला र संस्कृति संरक्षणमा स्थानीय युवाको सक्रियता उदाहरणीय छ ।

articles.title: माननीयको अभिब्यक्तिले सुरक्षा संगठनको बदनाम
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मुलुकको शान्ति, सुरक्षा र कानुन कार्यान्वयनको मुख्य जिम्मेवारी बोकेको नेपाल प्रहरी अहिले दोहोरो दबाबमा परेको छ । एकातिर गत बर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गतेको आन्दोलनका क्रममा संगठनले भोगेको भौतिक तथा मनोवैज्ञानिक क्षतिको असर अझै पूर्णरूपमा मेटिन सकेको छैन भने, अर्कोतिर राजनीतिक वृत्तबाटै संगठनको नेतृत्व र कार्यशैलीमाथि प्रश्न उठाउने क्रम तीव्र बनेको छ ।

राज्यकै प्रमुख निकायहरु कार्यपालिका र ब्यवस्थापिकाबाटै प्रहरी संगठनको बदनाम गर्ने कार्यले संगठनको मनोबल झनै गिराएको छ । सार्वजनिक पदमा बसेका व्यक्तिले उठाउने प्रश्नले सधैं सार्वजनिक चासो निम्त्याउँछ, विशेषगरी त्यो प्रश्न राज्यको कुनै संवेदनशील निकायविरुद्ध उठाइएको हुँदा गत बुधबार सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको बैठकमा रास्वपाका सांसद खगेन्द्र सुनारले नेपाल प्रहरीको सामग्री खरिद प्रक्रियामा प्रश्न उठाउँदै प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई नै कठघरामा उभ्याए ।

जुत्ता, मोजा, पोशाकदेखि लाठी खरिदसम्ममा आर्थिक अनियमितता भएको आशय दिँदै उनले तत्काल निष्पक्ष छानबिनको माग गरे । आइजीपी कार्कीले तत्काल प्रतिवाद गरे । खरिद प्रक्रियामा कुनै अनियमितता नभएको दाबी गर्दै तथ्यहीन आरोप लगाएर कर्मचारीको मनोबल कमजोर नबनाउन आग्रह गरे ।

त्यसपछि सांसद सुनारकै आफ्नै कानुनी पृष्ठभूमिबारे सार्वजनिक बहस सुरु भयो — प्रश्न उठाउने व्यक्ति स्वयं कति चोखो छ ? आईजीपी कार्कीले सांसद सुनारविरुद्ध नै आएका उजुरीहरूको चाङ औंल्याए । सुनारविरुद्ध माननीयदेखि दयनीयसम्मका व्यक्तिहरूले विभिन्न प्रकृतिका उजुरी दिएको र, आरोपको पोको खोलिदिन सक्ने चेतावनी दिए ।

सर्वत्र आलोचित खगेन्द्र अझै ‘अराजक’

लेखा समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीमाथि खगेन्द्र सुनारले उठाएको प्रश्नले मात्रै खगेन्द्र चर्चा र विवादमा आएका होइनन् । प्रहरी संगठन विरुद्ध पटक पटक सार्वजनिक उनको अभिब्यक्तिले सांसद सुनार आलोचित छन् ।

२०८३ वैशाख ७ गते सिन्धुली सुनकोशी गाउँपालिका–३ जुम्लीडाँडा निवासी २३ वर्षीय श्रीकृष्ण विक खुर्कोटस्थित प्रहरीको हिरासतमै मृत्यु भएको घटनामा जनप्रतिनिधिको हैसियतमा सिन्धुली पुगेका सुनाले एकतर्फी आरोप लगाउँदै सिन्धुलीका एसपीको कठालो नै समातेर घिसार्नुपर्ने अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए ।

सांसद हुनुपूर्व सुनारले एक वर्षअघि माइतीघरबाट समेत जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसर काठमाडौंका एकजना डीएसपी विरुद्ध अर्मयादित अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए । त्यो बेला जहाँ पनि उनी हातमा नेल र निधारमा नवसेना लेखिएको फेटा बाँधेर सांकेतिक विरोधमा देखिन्थे । यो पटक संसदीय समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीविरुद्ध पनि उही शैलीमा आक्रोश पोखेका थिए ।

सुनारविरुद्ध तीन मुद्दा अदालतमा विचाराधिन

सांसद खगेन्द्र माथि अहिले पनि तीनवटा मुद्दा अदालतमै विचाराधीन छ । दैलेखको नारायण नगरपालिका–२ भैसेखोरका खगेन्द्र प्रतिनिधि सभाको चुनावमा भने बाँके क्षेत्र नम्बर ३ बाट निर्वाचित भएका हुन् । उनीमाथि सुर्खेत प्रहरीले २०८० को असारमा पक्राउ गरेर सार्वजनिक शान्तिविरुद्धको कसुरमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

त्यो बेला जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय सुर्खेतले २० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी लिएर छाडेको थियो । त्यसको एक वर्षपछि पुनः २०८१ असारमै सुर्खेतकै अस्पतालका डाक्टरहरुमाथि अभद्र व्यवहार तथा तोडफोडको मुद्दा हाल सुर्खेत जिल्ला अदालतमा विचाराधीन अवस्थामा छ । २०८२ साउनमा काभ्रेकी एक महिलामाथि सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत चरित्र हत्या गर्ने खालको पोष्ट गरेको आरोपमा उनीमाथि काभ्रे प्रहरीले साइबर अपराधमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

साउन ५ गते पक्राउ पुर्जी लिए पनि उनी पक्राउ भने परेनन् । पछि मुद्दा अदालत दर्ता भएपछि उनी काभ्रे जिल्ला अदालतमा हाजिर भएका थिए । काभ्रे अदालतले समेत सुनारलाई ५० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी बुझाएर मात्रै छाड्ने आदेश गरेका थिए । हालसम्म पनि मुद्दा टुंगो लागेको छैन ।

सुनारको प्रहरी नेतृत्वमाथि भएको व्यक्तिगत आक्षेप र अमर्यादित व्यवहार विवाद गृहमन्त्री हुँदै सभामुखसम्म पुगेको छ । आइजिपीसहित आठ एआइजी र एक डिआइजीले प्रहरी संगठनकै मनोबल खस्किएको भन्दै संसदीय छानबिनमा विधि र मर्यादा पालना गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन् ।

बेनामे उजुरीको भरमा संसदीय समितिमा बोलाएर संगठनकै मानमर्दन हुने गरी हुर्मत लिएको गुनासो समेत गरेका छन् । प्रहरी अधिकारी मात्र होइन, गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङसमेत सुनारको ब्यवहारले रुष्ट छन् ।

प्रहरी संगठनबाटै ‘माननीय’विरुद्ध खेद ब्यक्त

प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्य सुनारको अराजक अभिब्यक्तिको सिंगो प्रहरी संगठनले नै खेद प्रकट गरेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरी पूर्वप्रहरी संगठन प्रमुख मञ्चले विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर सुरक्षा निकाय र यसको नेतृत्वमाथि भएका व्यक्तिलक्षित टीकाटिप्पणीप्रति खेद प्रकट गरेको छ ।

भने पूर्वप्रहरी कर्मचारी परिषद्, पूर्वसशस्त्र प्रहरी संघ र सुरक्षा तथा न्याय अध्ययन केन्द्रले संयुक्त विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर यस्ता गतिविधिले सुरक्षाकर्मीको मनोबल खस्कने र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामै असर पर्ने स्पष्ट गरेका छन् । साथै ती संस्थाहरूले संसदीय समितिमा बोलाउँदा पदीय गरिमा, सम्मान र व्यावसायिक मर्यादा कायम राख्न सुझाएका छन् ।

अझै पुरिएको छैन भदौ २४ को घाउ

नेपाल प्रहरीका लागि २०८२ भदौ २३ र २४ गते घटनाको घाउ अझै पुरिएको छैन । त्यो घटनाले संगठनको भौतिक संरचना, हतियार, कार्यालय र प्रहरी कर्मचारीको सुरक्षामाथि नै ठूलो चुनौती खडा गरेको छ ।

उक्त आन्दोलनका क्रममा काठमाडौँ उपत्यकाका मात्र १ सय ५३ प्रहरी कार्यालयमा आगजनी, १७ वटा प्रहरी वृत्त क्षतिग्रस्त,१ हजार १ सय हतियार लुटिपाट,३ जना प्रहरीको मृत्यु र प्रहरी कर्मचारीले ज्यान जोगाउन बर्दी फुकालेर भाग्नुपर्ने अवस्था आएको थियो ।

सुरक्षा संगठन र कर्मचारीको मनोबल बढाउनुपर्नेमा सत्तारुढ दलबाट नै यस्ता खाले अभिव्यक्तिले संगठनको मनोबल गिर्दो अवस्थामा पुगेको पूर्व प्रहरी अधिकारीको भनाई छ ।

सांसदको काम प्रश्न उठाउनु नै हो, तर प्रश्न उठाउने नाममा प्रमाणविनाका आरोप लगाउनु र आरोप प्रमाणित नहुँदै त्यसलाई सत्यका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्नु जिम्मेवार राजनीतिक अभ्यास होइन । खगेन्द्र सुनार हिजो आन्दोलनकारी भए पनि आज जनताका प्रतिनिधि हुन् ।

त्यसैले विना आधार राज्यको जिम्मावार निकायहरुको बदनाम गर्दा सुरक्षा संगठनको मात्र होइन, स्वयम् माननीयको ओज घटाउँछ । प्रहरीलाई प्रश्न गरौँ, तर प्रमाणसहित ।

प्रहरीलाई जवाफदेही बनाऔँ, तर संस्थागत रूपमा । प्रहरी कमजोर हुँदा कमजोर हुने प्रहरी प्रमुख मात्र होइन, सिंगो राज्य हो । प्रहरी संगठनका भित्रका कमजोरीहरु सुधार हुनु पर्छ नै, सांसद सुनारको आफू पनि सुध्रिन जरुरी छ ।

articles.title: पूर्वी नाकाबाट विदेशी पर्यटक बढे, सबैभन्दा धेरै भुटानी
articles.summary:
झापा । पूर्वी नेपालको प्रमुख स्थलमार्ग काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा ८६ देशका ९ हजार ४४७ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल भित्रिएका छन्। अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाको तथ्याङ्कअनुसार यो संख्या दैनिक औसत करिब २६ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेको हो ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा काँकरभिट्टा नाकाबाट नेपाल प्रवेश गर्ने विदेशी पर्यटकमा भुटान, अमेरिका, थाइल्याण्ड, अष्ट्रेलिया, बेलायत, क्यानडा, जर्मनी, फ्रान्स, जापान र रुसलगायत देशका नागरिक छन् । कुल आगन्तुकमध्ये भुटानी नागरिकको हिस्सा सबैभन्दा ठूलो छ । ४ हजार ९९४ जना भुटानी नागरिक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् ।

जुन कुल पर्यटक संख्याको करिब ५३ प्रतिशत हो । त्यस्तै २ हजार १५२ जना अमेरिकी नागरिकले काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । यो कुल आगन्तुकको करिब २३ प्रतिशत हो । भारतका नागरिकलाई नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न भिसा आवश्यक नपर्ने भएकाले उनीहरूलाई तेस्रो मुलुकका पर्यटकसम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्कमा समावेश गरिएको छैन ।

महिनागत तथ्याङ्कअनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी विदेशी पर्यटक पुसमा १ हजार ८५० जना र सबैभन्दा कम भदौमा २१६ जना नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । अध्यागमन कार्यालयले पुस र माघलाई प्रमुख पर्यटकीय याम मानेको छ ।

पर्यटकको आगमन उत्साहजनक भएपनि बसाइ छोटो हुने गरेको होटल व्यवसायी बताउँछन। पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यमा पर्यटकलाई केही दिन रोक्न सके झापा, इलाम, ताप्लेजुङलगायत जिल्लाको पर्यटन तथा होटल व्यवसायमा उल्लेख्य योगदान पुग्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ छ ।

पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार र सीमा नाकामै यातायात, होटल तथा भ्रमणसम्बन्धी सूचना उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने पर्यटन व्यवसायी कुन्दन निरौला बताउँछन् ।

अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाले सन् २०२४ अगस्टदेखि पूर्ण रूपमा अध्यागमन सेवा सञ्चालन गरेको थियो । सेवा प्रभावकारी भएपछि विदेशी पर्यटकको आगमन क्रमशः बढेको सूचना अधिकारी इन्द्रकुमार राजवंशी बताउँछन् ।

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार, पर्यटन सूचना केन्द्र र आकर्षक प्याकेज निर्माणसँगै संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहबीच समन्वय गर्न सके विदेशी पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउन सकिने देखिन्छ । यसबाट होटल, यातायात, ट्राभल्स, हस्तकला तथा स्थानीय उत्पादनको बजारसमेत लाभान्वित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: राँगाको सिङबाट बन्ने गुँला पर्वको मुख्य बाजा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेवार समुदायका विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीको प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक पर्व गुँला बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । एक महिनासम्म मनाइने पर्वमा भक्तजनले परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित चैत्य, विहार र मन्दिरको परिक्रमा गर्दै बुद्धको पूजा–आराधना गर्ने गर्दछन् ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका परम्परागत नेवार वस्ती र टोलहरुमा अब एक महिनासम्म सडक वा गल्लीहरुमा विहान मानिसहरुको चहलपहल शुरु नहुँदै सुनिने छ, धिमे, भुस्या, बाँसुरी र न्याकुँको सुमधुर आवाज । अनि बाजाको यही धुन पछ्याउँदै मानिसहरू चैत्यतर्फ अघि बढिरहेका हुने छन् । यो गुँला पर्वको अवसरमा देखिने दृश्य हो ।

नेवार समुदायमा पनि विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीले मनाउने गुँला पर्व बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि भाद्र शुक्ल प्रतिपदासम्म चल्ने यो पर्व करिब एक महिनासम्म धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।

गुँला शब्दको अर्थ आफैमा रोचक पनि छ । नेपाल भाषामा ‘गुँ’ को अर्थ नौ र ‘ला’ को अर्थ महिना भन्ने गरिन्छ । नेपाल संवतको नवौँ महिनामा मनाइने भएकाले यसको नाम गुँला रहन गएको मानिन्छ । गुँलाको वास्तविक आकर्षण बिहानै सुरु हुने यात्रामा देखिन्छ । भक्तजनहरू परम्परागत बाजा बजाउँदै विभिन्न चैत्य, विहार, बहाः र बहीको परिक्रमा गर्छन् ।

काठमाडौंको स्वयम्भू, बौद्ध, पाटनलगायतका धार्मिक तथा ऐतिहासिक स्थलमा गुँला पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखिन्छ । एउटा समूह धिमे बजाउँदै अघि बढिरहेको हुन्छ । यसमा कसैले भुस्या बजाइरहेको हुन्छ भने कसैले न्याकुँको गहिरो आवाज निकालिरहेको हुन्छ । यही दृश्यले गुँलालाई काठमाडौँका अन्य धेरै जात्रा र पर्वहरुभन्दा फरक बनाएको छ ।

गुँला पूजा र परिक्रमा गर्ने पर्व मात्रै होइन । संगीत जोडिएको उपत्यकाको जीवित संस्कृति पनि हो । विशेषगरी न्याकुँ बाजा गुँलाको पहिचानसँग जोडिएको छ । राँगाको सिङबाट बनाइने यो बाजा हेर्दा साधारण देखिए पनि यसको ध्वनि निकै विशिष्ट हुन्छ ।

परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक यात्राहरुमा यसको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ । त्यसैगरी धिमे, बाँसुरी, भुस्या र धाः लगायतका बाजासँगै बज्दा यी आवाजले पनि गुँला पर्वमा सांगीतिक समूहको स्वरूप लिन्छन् । पछिल्लो समय यस्ता जात्रा पर्वमा नयाँ पुस्ताको सहभागिता पनि बढिरहेको छ । नयाँ पूस्ताको सहभागितासँगै परम्परागत पर्व र संस्कृति पुस्तान्तरण पनि हुँदैछन् ।

गुँला धार्मिक पर्व मात्रैमा सीमित छैन । सामाजिकरुपमा खेतीपातीको मुख्य काम सकिएको समयसँग पनि यो पर्व जोडिएको छ । मानिसहरू केही फुर्सदिला हुने यही समयमा समुदाय भेला हुने, भेटघाट गर्ने र सामूहिक रूपमा धार्मिक गतिविधिमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पनि गुँलाले जुटाइ दिएको छ ।

बौद्ध परम्परामा वर्षायामको साधना र धार्मिक अभ्याससँग पनि गुँला समयको सम्बन्ध जोडिन्छ । त्यसैले यो अवधि पूजा, ध्यान, पाठ, दान र पुण्यकर्मका लागि विशेष मानिन्छ । यसको अर्को पक्ष के भने गुँला पर्वमा हुने चैत्य परिक्रमा एउटा यात्रा मात्रै होइन ।

उपत्यकाका विभिन्न स्थानीय धार्मिक स्थललाई जोड्ने सांस्कृतिक नेटवर्क जस्तो पनि हो । एउटा टोलबाट अर्को टोल, एउटा बहाःबाट अर्को चैत्यसम्म बाजाको धुनले यी ठाउँहरूलाई जोडिरहेको हुन्छ । काठमाडौंलाई मन्दिरै–मन्दिरको सहर भनिन्छ । तर गुँला पर्वले कामठाडौँ बाजा, बहाः, बही र चैत्यहरूको पनि सहर हो भन्ने प्रमाण पनि दिन्छ । एक महिनासम्म बज्ने यी बाजाहरु पुर्खाको स्मृति हुन्, धार्मिक आस्था हुन् र पहिचानको आवाज हुन् ।

articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: Nepal’s crackdown on businessmen can’t have it both ways
articles.summary:
In early May, days after Shekhar Golchha was arrested, the Supreme Court found his detention illegal, explicitly citing the bypassing of due process. But within hours of his release, a team from the Central Investigation Bureau rearrested him on a separate insurance-fraud allegation. A CIB official told reporters the new case was entirely unrelated to the one the court had just thrown out. Last month, Golchha was released on bail for Rs10 million.

It’s a small scene, but it captures something the Balendra Shah administration hasn’t resolved yet. A government can pursue accountability and still overreach. The question is whether this one can tell the difference — and whether it can keep doing both at once.

Nepal’s arrests and legal charges against high-profile businessmen — from Shankar Agrawal to Shekhar Golchha to Prithvi Bahadur Pande — are starting to resemble a crackdown that took the business world by storm almost ten years ago. In February 2017, days after youth-led protests had helped force South Korean President Park Geun-hye’s impeachment, Samsung heir Lee Jae-yong was arrested on charges of bribing Park and her confidante in exchange for government support for a merger. Lee was convicted, imprisoned and later pardoned. A separate set of charges tied to the merger itself dragged on for years, ending only in 2025 when South Korea’s Supreme Court upheld his acquittal.

The point is not that Nepal is South Korea, or that Golchha is Lee. The comparison is about something more basic: what prolonged legal uncertainty can do to business decision-making, even in a country with far stronger institutions. The cost of those years of jeopardy surrounding one of South Korea’s flagship companies made headlines across major business publications. Bloomberg’s own editorial board made a version of this argument in January 2017, before Lee’s conviction — that punishing one executive wouldn’t fix what actually needed reforming. Samsung subsequently shelved the internal “Future Strategy Office” that had coordinated group-wide decisions, while major investment and M&A decisions remained constrained. When Lee was finally cleared of the merger-related charges in 2025, the end of that legal uncertainty was seen as a positive for the company.

Nepal’s version may not appear as acute right now. But the quieter concern spreading through the business community is more consequential than a few angry statements from businessmen: people are beginning to ask what kinds of ordinary commercial decisions can expose them to criminal investigation. FNCCI, CNI and the Nepal Chamber of Commerce issued a joint statement after Golchha’s arrest, conceding plainly that the private sector has no disagreement that anyone found guilty should be held accountable, while asking the government to listen first and not treat detention as the default response to an allegation; guilt after all is a matter for the courts to establish. A new Asset Investigation Commission, established primarily to target politicians and bureaucrats, has pulled in private board members over their roles in institutions such as SEBON and Nepal Telecom.

Underneath the personnel churn, however, something more durable appears to be happening: the anti-graft body’s new national strategic plan extends anti-corruption law, for the first time, to private companies, cooperatives and banks directly. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle has framed the whole push in his own words, telling a Kathmandu audience the government is working to dismantle institutional capture and the collusion between business interests and corrupt politicians, and has urged the private sector not to protect wrongdoing.

Wagle’s argument is not hard to understand. Nepal has a long history of business-politician entanglements, and businesses should not be above the law. But there is a crucial distinction between investigating corruption and making legitimate commercial risk look like criminal conduct after the fact. A commercial decision that turns out badly, or even one that raises regulatory questions, does not by itself establish a criminal offence. There should be a credible basis for treating conduct as potentially criminal before a criminal investigation is launched, and the fact that an investigation is warranted does not, by itself, mean that the person under investigation must be arrested or detained. The latter can change how an entire economy behaves.

The newest frontier of this is the loan itself. At a meeting with Wagle this month, the chief executives of 20 commercial banks told him their staff was growing afraid to lend. Nepal Bankers’ Association President Santosh Koirala put it to the finance minister directly: bankers fear they could be arrested simply for extending loans or making investments. Whether those fears are ultimately borne out in any particular case is for the courts and investigators to establish. But the perception itself matters: if bankers begin to believe that commercially defensible decisions can later expose them to criminal liability, they will have the incentive to avoid decisions that lending requires.

The case of Nepal Investment Mega Bank is the most recent example of what many people see as government overreach. In 2025, NIMB auctioned defaulted telecom operator Smart Telecom’s collateral to Ncell, following a routine recovery procedure under banking rules when a borrower defaults. The CIB opened a case anyway, alleging collusion, and has since recommended prosecution of 22 people — executives and board members of NIMB and Ncell — over a claimed Rs95 billion loss.

Three former central bank governors, not otherwise aligned with each other, have all said that this is the central bank’s jurisdiction, not the CIB’s. But the issue need not be framed as a choice between the Nepal Rastra Bank and the CIB. The central bank has regulatory and supervisory responsibilities over banks, while the police can investigate suspected criminal conduct. The more important question is whether a disputed banking decision involves a regulatory breach, poor commercial judgment, or evidence of an actual criminal offence — and whether the institution investigating has a proper legal basis for doing that. One of the former governors, Chiranjibi Nepal, has summarised the cost of getting that wrong quite frankly: bankers should not be treated like criminals or murderers and subjected to arbitrary arrest.

The legal merits of the NIMB case will ultimately be decided by the courts. But the question for the government is broader than any one case: what message does an arrest send to the next banker asked to approve a difficult loan, or the next board member asked to make a commercially necessary decision?

As NEPSE continued to fall, Prime Minister Balendra Shah convened capital-market stakeholders directly, trying to talk it back up. We don’t know yet whether that intervention will work. But the fact that the prime minister felt the need to reassure investors is itself revealing.

Nepal wants more capital, more investment and more lending. It also wants to dismantle the networks of corruption that have distorted all three for the last three decades. Those goals are not inherently contradictory. What is contradictory is asking the same people to take economic risks while making them wonder whether those decisions could later become grounds for criminal prosecution. A government cannot extend an invitation for the same class of people for capital and prison time in the same news cycle and expect them to ignore the latter.

articles.title: No basic diet for young ANFA athletes
articles.summary:
On Wednesday morning, 19 children were having lunch—the humble dal-bhat-tarkari—in the dining hall of the hostel operated by the All Nepal Football Association in Satdobato, Lalitpur.

“We used to provide them with meat daily,” said Hira Pant, ANFA’s hostel in-charge. “Now, these children have to go to their school and sleep after eating only rice and lentils, not even vegetables.”

For the young academy players, the ANFA Complex in Lalitpur was supposed to be a place of refuge and recovery. The 19 children were relocated here two months ago, carrying the trauma of a tragedy that shook Nepali sports.

Until September 28, 2024, they had been living at the football academy in Sisneri, Makawanpur. That fateful day, six of their friends died in a landslide while fleeing their hostel building out of fear of rising floodwaters as the Kulekhani dam opened following heavy rain. The children were then relocated to Hetauda before they were brought to Satdobato.

While the six deceased children’s families are still awaiting a proper probe into the incident, those who survived want to carry their friends’ dreams as well. But they find themselves in a difficult situation, as there is not even a proper diet to sustain them.

“The breakfast menu had items like milk, eggs, cornflakes, muesli and sausage, among other protein-rich items,” Pant said. “The menu has been stripped down to black tea and plain biscuits for almost a month now.”

Why are children who were selected from across the country through ANFA’s grassroots programme being treated like this?

ANFA officials say the problem is a result of the FIFA suspension and the directive of the National Sports Council not to use their bank accounts for “any” purpose.

“Following the suspension, the National Sports Council issued a directive, instructing us to halt all activities and financial transactions,” said Suresh Shah, ANFA’s spokesperson. “As a result, our usual vendors—including suppliers like Salesberry—have stopped providing goods on credit.”Alongside the 19 children, the hostel houses national team players recovering from injuries sustained in Bhutan.

Kantipur reached the ANFA Complex again in the evening, after the students returned from their school. The young athletes looked far from energetic. They needed permission to speak, but they all looked confused, probably questioning themselves of their choices.

Having already endured the trauma of losing six of their peers in the Sisneri landslide, being undernourished in a place meant to nurture their dreams has left a visible toll on them. With their daily routine stripped of basic athletic nutrition and their futures caught in an administrative gridlock between ANFA, the NSC and FIFA, the young players are left navigating an uncertainty far bigger than football.

So, how long does ANFA plan to let the children suffer?

“You would be better off directing this question to the government, because the answers lie with them,” Shah, the ANFA spokesperson, said. “In truth, ANFA has no leverage or control over the situation right now.”

Shah added that they are still fulfilling their duties by preparing for the U15 World Cup qualifiers. “We believe the government recognises the urgency,” he said. “Our understanding is that once the suspension is lifted, operations will resume in full force.”

Shah added that ANFA officials and executive members have been paying out of their pockets to buy the basic food and other items. “We have started buying from some other shops on credit,” Shah said. “We are even paying for water, which costs around Rs2,000 a tanker, every day.”

It is not only the children who have been affected. Pant, her employees, security guards and other officials have also been working without salary for a couple of months.

Amid this, Pant is handling the situation with quiet resignation. “We are continuing our work only to ensure that these children are not left abandoned,” she said.

articles.title: Lamichhane urges RSP lawmakers to uphold parliamentary decorum
articles.summary:
Rastriya Swatantra Party chair Rabi Lamichhane has urged the party’s lawmakers to maintain parliamentary decorum and conduct themselves with restraint in the House.

Lamichhane made the remarks at the RSP parliamentary party meeting on Wednesday.

He also advised lawmakers not to criticise opposition parties, saying they were simply carrying out their role as the opposition.

“Don’t criticise the opposition parties. They are doing their job as the opposition,” Lamichhane said.

Lamichhane said Prime Minister Balendra Shah would attend the next parliamentary party meeting. Shah is also the RSP’s parliamentary party leader.

“The prime minister will attend the next parliamentary party meeting. I have spoken to him about it. The next meeting will be held in the presence of the parliamentary party leader,” Lamichhane said. “Today’s meeting is an informal one with lawmakers and ministers.”

He also asked lawmakers to bring party-related concerns directly to him.

“Tell me about party matters. I will also handle them through the party secretariat,” he said.

The RSP parliamentary party meeting also delayed Wednesday’s House of Representatives session. The session, scheduled for 1pm, began shortly before the time of reporting.

articles.title: Satu makes a comeback as a healthy urban snack
articles.summary:
Durga Baral of Kathmandu Greenland says she gives satu to her daughters as a morning snack every day.

“It is not good to give children biscuits all the time. I usually give them satu as a snack,” she said.

Baral said she and other members of her family also consume satu.

“We buy satu from a farmhouse. We can see them making it right in front of us. That makes us trust the product, so we buy and eat it from there,” she said.

Made by combining roasted maize, soybeans, chickpeas and barley into a snack mix or a multigrain powder, satu was once a common source of nutrition, particularly for children and elderly people in villages.

In the modern era, however, the fibre-rich traditional food lost its charm as fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and packaged foods made their way into villages and quickly gained dominance.

Now, satu is finding favour among urban consumers as a healthy snack. Demand for satu began to grow in urban areas after the Covid pandemic, as people increasingly started looking for healthier diets.

Packets of different varieties of satu can now be found lined up in grocery stores, organic farmhouses and large marts across the Kathmandu valley. Producers say demand has also been growing in other urban areas, driven by busy lifestyles, growing health consciousness and the search for alternatives to junk food.

Asbin Sapkota is an engineer by profession, but the 37-year-old from Baglung runs Dhikijanto Pvt Ltd, one of the leading retail stores selling traditional foods in Banasthali, Kathmandu.

Sapkota and his friends jointly started the business in 2021. The store sells satu along with a variety of agricultural products.

“Nowadays, mixed and special varieties of satu are popular among customers. The special satu contains dry fruits such as almonds, cashews and walnuts as well.”

The startup has expanded beyond the Kathmandu valley and reached overseas.

Sapkota said the company sends satu to markets such as Biratnagar, Chitwan, Butwal and Pokhara. “It is not just in Nepal. Nepalis living in countries such as Australia and New Zealand also order satu,” he said.

Dhikijanto sells between 300 and 400 kilograms of satu a month. “Sometimes demand is much higher. Once, an organisation ordered 2,000 kilograms of satu at once for children’s nutrition,” Sapkota said.

Dhikijanto purchases grains from districts including Mustang, Rasuwa, Jumla, Mugu and Dolpa. Sapkota says the store stocks around 70 to 80 types of products, including buckwheat, millet, wheat and maize flour, chyankhla, lentils and various pulses, as well as potatoes and garlic from Mustang.

Another familiar name among satu enthusiasts is “Kainla Dai Ko Satu”, based in Kapan Dhungedhara.

Narayan Raj Chaulagain, known as “Kainla Dai”—a traditional Nepali birth-order name given to the fourth son in a large family—has been in the satu business for the past six years. In the early days, Chaulagain sold pulses, spices and other local products. As demand for satu began to grow, he started commercially producing the ordinary satu traditionally made in villages.

“We initially started the business by selling local pulses and spices,” he said.

Chaulagain produces different varieties of satu based on customer preferences. He says he sources maize, chickpeas and other pulses needed to make satu from local farmers whenever possible.

“We bring products from districts such as Dolakha, Sindhupalchok and Kavrepalanchok. During the off-season, we bring maize from the Tarai. Our objective is to promote local production,” he said.

Chaulagain has also observed that health-conscious customers have increasingly started consuming satu as a light meal. As the business has expanded, he says they have also focused on maintaining the quality of their satu.

“At first, we mixed the ingredients based on our own experience. Later, we began producing satu after conducting laboratory tests for protein, calories and carbohydrates,” he said. “We maintain the same quantity and quality every time we make satu.”

Based on sales and conversations with consumers, Chaulagain said satu is popular among people ranging from children to the elderly.

It has also become easier for businesses to promote their products in recent years. Chaulagain said orders often come after promotional content about their products is posted on social media.

“Because of social media, the business has started reaching customers across the country and Nepalis living abroad, beyond the local market. It makes us happy,” he said.

“Kainla Dai” produces around 100 kilograms of satu a day and employs five people. He said mixed satu is sold for Rs550 per kilogram, while barley and chickpea satu costs Rs300 per kilogram.

The production and sale of satu is no longer limited to small and cottage industries. Some businesses have begun producing it on an industrial scale and taking it to international markets.

Poshilo Foods Pvt Ltd, established by Prithvi Kalyan Parajuli in Pokhara-18 in 2021, has been producing satu. The company, which began operations with an investment of Rs10 million, recently expanded its production facility to Jhapa as well. The company exports its products to the United States via India. Through a partnership with exporter Manaram Group, a major exporter of dog chew to the US, Poshilo has carved out its own space in the international market.

During the Covid pandemic, Parajuli had completed his BBA in Business and Market Management. Rather than seeking a job, he aspired to start his own business.

After conducting market research for a year, he founded Poshilo Foods at the age of 23. He raised Rs10 million by selling shares, seeking family support and taking a bank loan.

The company began production with an initial output of 100 kg of satu on its first day.

Gradually, production increased to 150 kg, then 200 kg and eventually 400 kg.

According to Parajuli, between September 2025 and February 2026, more than 1.5 tonnes of satu were shipped to the United States, where it is now available in around 200 stores.

Panu Paudel, chief operating officer of Bhat-Bhateni Supermarket, Nepal’s largest supermarket chain, also says sales of satu are growing.

“Many people buy it to eat at home. People used to drink Coca-Cola, but now demand for mohi [buttermilk] has increased. Satu is also gaining popularity in a similar way,” he said.

Satu has emerged as an example of an effort to connect traditional food culture with the modern market.

Nutritionist Ruju Khadka says although satu can be beneficial for health, its quality, production process and consumption method are important.

“Satu is something we consume by mixing it directly in water rather than cooking it. Therefore, the most important things are its packaging and hygiene,” she said. “Nutritionally, satu contains protein, carbohydrates, fibre, small amounts of fat, iron, magnesium, potassium and other nutrients. But if something goes wrong during processing, its nutritional benefits may not be effective.”

Khadka says consumers should be particularly careful when eating satu containing a large number of ingredients.

“Each ingredient in a mixed satu has its own nutritional value. If it contains dry fruits, pumpkin seeds, maize, wheat and other ingredients, it can provide good overall nutrition,” she said. “But because all ingredients have different shelf lives, this needs to be taken into consideration during production.”

Khadka says satu can be consumed by people of all age groups, including children above six months, but the quantity needs to be adjusted.

“Children, older people and young adults all have different nutritional requirements. The amount of satu should be determined based on what else a person eats throughout the day and how much physical activity they engage in,” she said.

She advises people with certain health conditions to be particularly careful when consuming satu.

“If someone has gastritis, they should consume a very small amount of satu and do so carefully. For people with diabetes, satu containing a high proportion of maize or carbohydrates is not considered very suitable. In mixed satu, consumers should also pay attention to which ingredient is present in the highest proportion,” she said.

She also cautions against treating satu as a complete food or a substitute for a balanced diet.

“Satu is a good option, but it cannot be considered a complete source of nutrition,” she said. “It contains both carbohydrates and protein. Therefore, one should not consume large amounts of chickpea satu simply because it is considered a source of protein. Other sources of protein are also necessary.”

articles.title: Women face higher risk of death in Nepal’s tiger attacks
articles.summary:
Tigers attacked 245 people in Nepal between 2010 and 2024, killing 141 of them, with women facing a far higher risk of death than men, according to a new study published in the journal Ecology and Evolution.

Women accounted for just 85 of the attacks but 62 of the fatalities, giving them a fatality rate of more than 72 percent. Men, meanwhile, were attacked 160 times and suffered 79 deaths, putting their fatality rate at less than 50 percent.

The study also found that most attacks occurred not inside national parks but in the buffer zones and forests surrounding them, where local people regularly enter to collect firewood and fodder, graze livestock, gather other forest products and fish.

The findings come as recent attacks in Chitwan again highlight the risks faced by communities living alongside Nepal’s growing tiger population.

On August 16, 60-year-old Thakur Adhikari was injured in a tiger attack in Piple Deurali village of Rapti Municipality in eastern Chitwan. The tiger had strayed into the settlement and mauled Adhikari, leaving him with deep wounds to his leg. He is undergoing treatment at Bharatpur Hospital.

The same tiger had earlier attacked a cow in a nearby shed belonging to Dila Kumari Tamang.

Five days earlier, on August 12, Mangal Bote was killed by a tiger while inside a buffer zone forest in Meghauli, west of Chitwan National Park. Park authorities have since captured both tigers involved in the two incidents.

The latest attacks underscore a central finding of the study: people are far more likely to encounter tigers outside the core areas of national parks than inside them.

The paper was co-authored by researchers including Bed Kumar Dhakal, deputy director general and spokesperson at the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, and wildlife experts Baburam Lamichhane, Naresh Subedi, Thakur Silwal, and Sanjay Kandel.

“Our goal was to analyse the underlying factors driving the total number of attacks,” said Lamichhane, whose PhD research focuses on human-tiger conflict.

Women face greater risk of dying

The study found a striking difference in the outcomes of attacks involving men and women.

Of the 245 people attacked during the 15-year period, 160 were men and 85 were women. Yet the gap narrowed sharply when researchers looked at fatalities. Tigers killed 79 men and 62 women.

That means women, although accounting for only about a third of all attacks, represented nearly 44 percent of the deaths.

Researchers say the disparity needs further investigation, but body posture at the time of an attack may be an important factor.

Men entering forests are more commonly involved in activities such as livestock grazing, which require them to stand or walk. Women frequently crouch or bend down while cutting grass, collecting fodder or gathering firewood.

The study found that 44 of 59 people attacked while crouching or sitting died. Among 71 people attacked while standing or walking, 29 died.

Researchers believe that being upright may give people a better chance of spotting an approaching tiger, escaping or defending themselves.

“Body posture at the time of the encounter seems to play a major role,” Lamichhane said. “We plan to investigate the higher mortality rate among women in greater detail.”

The study did not establish posture as the sole cause of the difference, and researchers say further work is needed to understand the social, occupational and behavioural factors behind the higher female fatality rate.

Most attacks occur outside parks

Although national parks and protected areas are the primary habitats for wild tigers, only a small proportion of attacks occurred deep inside forests.

Just 16 of the 245 attacks recorded in the study, or about 6.5 percent, occurred inside national parks. Buffer zones accounted for 69.4 percent of all attacks.

The buffer zones are designed as transition areas between protected wildlife habitats and human settlements. But they are also important sources of forest resources for surrounding communities.

The study found that 78 people died while collecting fodder or firewood. Another 19 died while gathering non-timber forest products, 17 while grazing livestock, 11 while fishing and six during agricultural work.

The pattern points to the close link between human dependence on forests and the risk of encounters with tigers.

“Villagers should enter the woods in groups rather than alone, and avoid visits during early morning or evening hours when tigers are most active,” Lamichhane said.

He also recommended clearing dense vegetation along routes commonly used for collecting fodder and firewood. Better visibility could reduce the likelihood of sudden encounters and give people more time to respond when a tiger is nearby.

Dhakal recommended that community forests adopt block-based management, with people collecting forest resources in designated areas rather than moving randomly through dense vegetation.

“Managing designated blocks for resource collection ensures clear lines of sight, reducing the chances of accidental confrontations with tigers or rhinos,” Dhakal said.

Chitwan accounts for nearly half of attacks

Chitwan, which has Nepal’s largest tiger population, remains the country’s main hotspot for human-tiger conflict.

The district accounted for 47 percent of all recorded attacks during the 15-year study period. But the average annual death toll has declined compared with earlier years.

According to Lamichhane, an average of seven people died each year from tiger attacks between 1998 and 2006. That fell to about five deaths annually between 2010 and 2024.

The decline has come despite a substantial increase in Nepal’s tiger population.

The country’s latest tiger census put the wild population at 429, with 145 tigers living in Chitwan National Park alone.

No tiger-related fatalities were recorded in Chitwan’s buffer zone in the previous fiscal year, a significant improvement from a peak of 16 deaths in a single year. But recent incidents show that the risk remains acute, particularly in settlements and forests bordering the park.

The study also found geographical gaps in recorded attacks. No attacks were reported during the 15-year period in the lowland Tarai east of Rautahat or in Rupandehi and Kapilvastu, between Rautahat and Kanchanpur. Incidents were, however, recorded farther north in districts including Surkhet and Salyan.

Researchers say authorities must also monitor individual tigers that pose a higher risk to people.

Older, injured or otherwise weakened tigers can struggle to hunt wild prey and may move closer to settlements in search of easier food.

Lamichhane said regular monitoring and the timely rescue of such animals are critical to preventing attacks. Chitwan National Park has maintained an active tiger rescue programme for the past six years.

But researchers say removing individual problem tigers (that repeatedly attack people) alone cannot address the broader causes of conflict.

Much of the risk arises because people continue to enter forests for basic needs, particularly in buffer zones and community forests.

Reducing that dependence will require alternative sources of energy and income, as well as safer ways of accessing forest resources, Lamichhane said.

Communities seek a bigger conservation share

People living around national parks bear much of the cost of wildlife conservation, local officials say, and need greater economic benefits from the presence of protected wildlife.

Dhakal, who is pursuing a doctorate on human-tiger conflict, said buffer zone communities should receive more support for alternative income-generating activities.

Local committees in Chitwan already run programmes aimed at reducing dependence on forests and improving coexistence with wildlife.

Shivaji Gayak, chairman of the Chitwan National Park Buffer Zone Management Committee, said user committees conduct awareness campaigns, distribute gas stoves to reduce the need to collect firewood, provide grass seed for livestock and promote homestays and other forms of ecotourism.

But funding remains a major constraint.

Under park regulations, 30 to 50 percent of national park revenue is supposed to be allocated to buffer zone user committees. Chitwan has 21 such committees and one sub-committee.

Gayak said the amount actually reaching the committees is significantly lower than the statutory share.

“Although park revenues exceed Rs300 million, buffer zone committees receive only Rs60 million to Rs80 million, well below the statutory percentage,” he said.

The shortfall limits their ability to improve forest management, expand awareness campaigns and support communities facing wildlife attacks, Gayak said.

articles.title: RSP must turn its parliamentary initiative into results
articles.summary:
Last week, a meeting of the House of Representatives scheduled to discuss a bill was adjourned due to the absence of the minimum number of lawmakers required to conduct the meeting. Nepal’s statute requires at least one-fourth of the total strength, or 69 lawmakers, to be present for a House meeting to commence. However, only 61 lawmakers were present, prompting the Speaker to adjourn the meeting. While it is the responsibility of every lawmaker to ensure regular attendance, the onus of ensuring that the House functions smoothly lies with the ruling party. The Rastriya Swatantra Party commands 182 seats, which is two and a half times the minimum number required for the House to get down to business.

It was complete negligence on the part of a party with close to a two-thirds majority to leave Parliament without the minimum presence of lawmakers just four months after the House began its work. Even though this was the first such incident involving the full House, meetings of House committees have previously been postponed for the same reason.

However, in a timely intervention, the party is taking serious measures to ensure that its lawmakers do not merely mark their attendance and skip House proceedings. It has asked every lawmaker to fill out a Google Form providing details of their attendance and to notify the party in advance if they cannot attend a meeting. The party leadership believes the move will make parliamentary meetings more organised and effective, and rightly so.

The RSP rose to power by capitalising on the ineffective performance of the legacy parties on multiple fronts, including Parliament. The two previous HoRs elected after the promulgation of the Constitution of Nepal were not productive. The internal feud within the then Nepal Communist Party disrupted the functioning of the House elected in 2017. Then Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli dissolved the House twice, effectively cutting its working period by about a year. The House elected in 2022 also became mired in repeated obstruction. The Nepali Congress blocked proceedings for weeks, demanding a probe into RSP chair Rabi Lamichhane’s alleged involvement in cooperative fraud. The RSP later obstructed the House, seeking an investigation into the visit visa scam, while the CPN-UML did the same over alleged gold smuggling.

That House eventually met an early demise following its dissolution after the Gen Z protests in September. Most of the tenure of previous two Houses was spent in the making and unmaking of governments, with less focus on its core job of enacting laws and holding fruitful discussions.

As a result, the previous Houses could not even promulgate the laws necessary for the full-fledged implementation of the Constitution. History should not repeat itself. The third House since the promulgation of the Constitution needs to correct the shortcomings of its predecessors. The initiative the RSP is taking to keep track of its lawmakers’ attendance is a positive step towards that effort.

The Balendra Shah government has set a target of promulgating 166 laws through Parliament in the current fiscal year. Making that happen requires effective functioning of Parliament and its mini-Houses—the parliamentary committees. That, in turn, requires the active participation of lawmakers and proper facilitation by the government. The RSP leadership seems to have understood this fact. Now, it needs to translate that understanding into implementation.

articles.title: The relentless cycle of politics as usual
articles.summary:
It has been nearly a year since the Gen Z movement, and seems like we are back to square one. And it is not only the return of Sher Bahadur Deuba or KP Sharma Oli’s steadfast refusal to brook any dissent in the CPN–UML that is responsible for this sense of déjà vu. Look around you—much of it looks and also feels the same.

For instance, not to take things lying down just because they are out of power in Kathmandu, the older political parties are back to their usual selves of pulling down governments and cobbling together new ones. Every provincial government, barring Gandaki’s, has faced a crisis since the disruptions of last September. Oli and his bête noire-cum-best friend, Pushpa Kamal Dahal, the ‘coordinator’ of the Nepali Communist Party (NCP), have joined forces to rejig some provincial coalitions. One does feel for Oli’s true bête noire, Madhav Kumar Nepal, the ‘co-coordinator’ of the same NCP, who could but whimper in protest against Dahal’s machinations.

In contrast, the Nepali Congress under Gagan Thapa has taken a principled position: it will not form alliances that leave legislative bodies without a meaningful opposition. But that is not likely to prevent others from toppling Congress governments. One of only two such Congress worthies, the chief minister of Madhesh, Krishna Prasad Yadav, took office in December last year at the head of a seven-party bloc, consisting of the Congress plus the JSP, the JP, the LSP and the NUP along with the Maoists and the CPN-S. With the latter two having merged as the Dahal-led NCP and the Oli-Dahal juggernaut on the roll, it may soon be only a matter of time before the Congress chief minister in Madhesh finds himself booted out.

If all these party acronyms are head-spinning, consider this septet: the JSP, the JP, the NUP, the PLP, the NSP(NSP), the AJP and the BEP, which have come together as yet another seven-party alliance, and at whose pleasure the Congress chief minister in Madhesh stays in office even if the seven-headed leadership has not broached the idea of government change. I have not even bothered to spell out the names of these parties in full as that is quite immaterial. Not only because most are bit players in the political firmament but also because the acronyms can change with each gust blowing the party supremos (a standing all seven have in common) hither or thither, and keeping track of every new development is a bother not worth taking.

Rocking horse rhythm

While the behaviour of the oldies is becoming progressively more depressing, what of the new messiah, i.e., Balendra Shah? Nothing, actually, since we know barely anything of his goings and comings or of his doings, apart from brief cameos on social media occasionally. Where no one could get Oli to shut up, the entire might of Nepal’s sovereign parliament has not been able to get a word out of Shah, barring that one disastrous performance during his impromptu Q&A.

Since Shah has finally been convinced that, as the country’s chief executive, isolation from the world is not wholly advisable, he has begun occasional parleys. One does wonder, though, what he manages to actually say in private, particularly in meetings with foreign officials. I certainly would have loved to peek into the briefs sent by the Indian and Chinese ambassadors back home on their impressions of our prime minister, a political novice if there was one. If the American embassy cables available thanks to WikiLeaks are any guide, the ambassadorial reports are likely to have had much to say, like the one describing Sher Bahadur Deuba as “affable” with a “non-confrontational demeanor” but also with “an apparent speech impediment [that] makes Deuba difficult to understand in any language”.

I would also have liked to look at the ambassadors’ assessments of the current state of affairs in the country. Consider the following US embassy report from March 1974, entitled ‘Birendra’s First Two Years’, which resonates somewhat uncannily with what is going on. “Bureaucrats, intelligentsia and urban elites have begun to weary of constant exhortation from the palace in the face of shortages, inflation and overall stagnation of the economy. Two years ago, these same groups, unrealistically taking the king's statements at face value, hoped for rapid and dramatic accomplishments from Birendra’s reign…Birendra has retained around him the same relatively inexperienced group of palace advisors with which he began…Politicians remain powerless and ineffective; the civil service is increasingly removed from the seat of power, and the palace secretariat is now the centre for all major decisions”.

Despite the initial flurry, it turns out the Balendra Shah government has been all movement and little action. There are decisions galore waiting to be taken but seemingly not within the priority of the prime minister and members of his cabinet. An earlier prime minister in a similar situation had done the country wrong through similar inaction. I am referring to an equally strong Oli at the head of a parliamentary supermajority. Not much action and all talk. Spending hours on end pontificating on everything under the sun during the day and scrolling through social media in the evening, Oli spent less time governing and more time conspiring to stay in power and spewing nonsense on the side. The result has been a federalisation process that remains incomplete more than a decade since the drafting of our new constitution and constant changes of governments in the centre and the provinces.

I have written in the past that there is little to choose between KP Sharma Oli and Balendra Shah. I was referring to their respective authoritarian style, complete lack of self-awareness, and absence of any humility. I did not realise that disinterest in governing was also something they had in common. For, like Oli and his penchant for social media, our current prime minister apparently spends his evenings playing video games. One understands everyone needs some downtime, but a country facing multiple crises can scarcely afford a head of government who tunes out every evening.

Going by his return to politics the moment he stepped back into Nepal, I wonder if Deuba really believes that he has a chance at electoral redemption. Time may not be on his side, but that has not stopped him from engaging in a gambit he should know very well is a dangerous one—that of championing the majority religion. Although the discovery of his religious self does not appear to be any new stance of his, having come out so openly and so strongly in favour of an intolerant form of Hinduism, he has shown himself more interested in his own political survival than the good of the country.

If, as they say, politics is the last refuge of scoundrels, I wonder what would best describe those who practice its most heinous form—the politics of religion. Find the term and apply that to Deuba.

articles.title: What the US FMF grant means for Nepal’s fleet
articles.summary:
In June, Nepal accepted a$100 million (around Rs15 billion) Foreign Military Financing (FMF) grant from the US to boost the country’s disaster response and humanitarian assistance capabilities. Nepal remains highly vulnerable to climate-induced disasters, including flash floods, wildfires, landslides and glacier lake outburst floods, making rapid aerial response a critical national priority. Under the grant, the country will receive six Bell helicopters comprising four Bell 407GXis and two Bell 412EPXs equipped for firefighting and external sling missions with a maximum payload of 2,268 kilograms. The new platforms are, realistically, expected to be delivered only after 2030. The Nepali Army already operates Bell variants, making them a logical addition that builds on existing operational familiarity.

The FMF grant contributes to Nepal’s disaster response posture but highlights a broader structural challenge associated with foreign security assistance for long-term use. The package’s initial spare parts, logistical support and training provisions facilitate early-stage operational readiness. However, long-term aircraft availability relies on Nepal’s ability to finance sustainment, develop local technical expertise, strengthen international supply chains and institutionalise lifecycle planning, while working with limited budgetary and institutional resources.

The Nepali Army already possesses a relatively capable aviation fleet for disaster response and humanitarian assistance, performing a broad range of missions, including search and rescue (SAR), medical evacuation (MEDEVAC), relief-material transport and humanitarian logistics. The fleet includes the Russian Mi-17 heavy-lift helicopter, the Indian HAL Dhruv Mk III light helicopter, the French Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil, the Polish PZL M28 Skytruck short-takeoff-and-landing (STOL) aircraft, among other complementary assets.

The fleet composition reflects decades of acquisition from multiple international partners under various procurement arrangements, consistent with Nepal’s long-standing non-alignment foreign policy posture. The planned addition of Bell helicopters further diversifies the country’s supplier base but simultaneously adds to the complexity of an already fragmented maintenance ecosystem. Each platform relies on its own maintenance procedures, technical documentation, spare parts supply chain, certification standards and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) support arrangements. This fragmented ecosystem exposes Nepal’s aircraft availability to disruptions across multiple supply chains and requires the Nepal Army to bear greater financial burdens and administrative complexity to support fleet readiness.

Nepal’s experience with the Mi-17 fleet illustrates the intricacy of maintaining foreign-origin aircraft throughout operational lifecycles. Two of the Nepali Army’s four Mi-17 helicopters have been stranded in India for more than two years. Due to the Russo-Ukrainian war, Nepal routed Mi-17 overhauls through the Indian state-owned Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), which subsequently subcontracted the work to the Vietnamese Helicopter Technical Service Company (HELITECHO). However, as the war lengthened and evolved, Russia revoked HELITECHO’s authorisation. Rosoboronexport, the official exporter of the Mi-17s, subsequently informed Nepal that overhauls carried out at a now-unauthorised facility cannot be certified as flight-safe.

Despite investing approximately $3.5 million in maintenance, the Mi-17s remain grounded. Russia’s stricter export-control posture has made it nearly impossible to obtain the necessary certification to fly the helicopters back to Nepal.
